title: What makes a strategy great: six traits of a "how we will win" document
summary: Jason Cohen argues that strategy is simply "how we will win," and that most documents titled strategy are vague wishful thinking. He lays out six traits of great strategy (simple, candid, decisive, leveraged, asymmetric, futuristic), with examples like Craigslist, Zappos and Amazon, plus tell-tale signs of bad strategy.

principles.text: Strategy must be simple, even simplistic, because no one reads or remembers long documents; it exists so everyone can make aligned daily decisions.
principles.quote: No one reads anything. You're in the Top 1% just for reading this sentence. No one remembers anything. Certainly not an 86-slide PowerPoint.

principles.text: Real threats are specific, present-tense and data-backed, not generic 'could happen' worries; a strategy that skips the scary facts is wrong.
principles.quote: Real threats are either happening now or are at least 70% likely to happen.

principles.text: Decide who you target and who you ignore, and accept the negative consequences up front so complaints from non-target customers don't derail you.
principles.quote: When those consequences inevitably arise, the team must be able to say "we expected that" rather than "we have to address that" or even "this is a signal that the strategy is wrong."

principles.text: Use the Opposite Test: a real strategic decision has a rational opposite that other successful companies have chosen; 'customer-first' fails it.
principles.quote: deciding to be open source is strategic, because plenty of companies are successful with a closed-source strategy. However, deciding to be "customer-first" is not a serious decision

principles.text: Leverage existing strengths and avoid weaknesses rather than trying to fix them; better still if the strength is differentiated and durable.
principles.quote: Great strategy leverages the strengths and assets of the organization; a bad strategy asks the organization to win even while acting unnaturally, often under the cover of "overcoming weaknesses."

principles.text: Build asymmetric bets where upside far exceeds downside, so the plan wins even with bad luck; a plan where everything must go right will fail.
principles.quote: If everything has to go right for the plan to succeed, it won't succeed.
